What to record: Identify the released project, material batch, and cut-list revision.
Record who set up and ran the process plus the production date.
Identify machine, blade, bit, cutter, jig, or program version.
State the face, edge, fence, stop, datum, or coordinate origin.
Example: Show face up / factory left edge

What to record: Record file name, checksum or version, postprocessor, and approved drawing.
Record stock size, face, origin, spoilboard, clamps, vacuum zones, and keep-outs.
Record tool numbers, measured diameters, stickout, paths reviewed, and collision result.
Record start/end, completed, held, rejected, rerun parts, and remaining stock.
